ratings_why.fun: Lots of real ordering puzzles that overlap: Squall Gusts at Start of Combat also hurry Late arrivals in, which fire Sir Vane and The Helm, while Black Cloud and the Duke pull in opposite directions; a few timing rules still need pinning down.
ratings_why.distinct: Over a 7 because the hand becomes a reserve board that enemy Start of Combat can't touch, timed by counting attacks; no current tribe or typical auto-battler tribe plays the hand during the fight.

verdict_why: The engine is good; a few timing rules (Sir Vane's pointer, what counts toward Lady High Pressure's sixth attack, Mrs Foul when Mr Fair is dead) need writing down before it plays as written.

points.text: Sir Vane points at the last unit you played, but a Late arrival also turns him. Say whether that turn lasts past the fight, or he points at a hand-only Courier next Start of Combat.
Lady High Pressure holds Gusts, but Late arrivals and her sixth-attack break both count attacks. Say whether held Gusts count toward the six, and whether arrivals after the storm are held again.
Mr Fair: say what Mrs Foul does if Mr Fair is already dead or has been lifted out, and whether his going indoors loses his hero-damage count.

Beacon-Keeper plus Gust Pages and Vane can reach three Gusts during Start of Combat, so Late units land before the first normal swing. Lean into it: one card that pays off a Late unit landing before any enemy attack.
The Sí Gaoithe's drop-back after your third attack is the same clock as Late. A line that lets a lifted enemy land on your side's count (or Gust when it returns) would tie it into the court's timing.

standouts.why: Duke Cumulonimbus turns a fight's tempo into stats, and Black Cloud and the Squall both change his count, so every Late build has a real choice.
Lady High Pressure ties both keywords into one held storm, and front row versus back row changes when it breaks.
Master of the Wild Hunt makes the dead count as arrivals, so Vane, The Helm and Black Cloud all fire again: the best hidden overlap in the set.

weakest.why: Windhover is a plain once-a-fight counter with nothing else to do with it.
Dew-Pond Heron repeats the Gust counter onto the biggest unit; it adds no decision the Tower and Föhn don't.
Keeper of the Glass is a threshold the Squall build hits anyway, so it's a gold tax rather than a choice.

flags.note: With the Steward, held Gusts happen four times, nine with goldens; worth the owner's eye for one-sided wipes.
Black Cloud's permanent +2/+2 per arrival stacks every fight on hand-held Late units and on every Wild Hunt revival.
What Sir Vane points at after a fight where a Late unit turned him.
"Never lands" but arrives in a slot mid-fight; say it can't be played while recruiting, and what 'nearest' means for its Gust.
